# index.html.md

<a id="manual-index"></a>

# XDMOD Manual

**XDMOD** (Cross-Domain MODeling) is a method plus tools for developing a product across systems
engineering, software, electronics and mechanics, in many git repos, with people and AI agents
working side by side. It is built on SYSMOD and SysML v2 for the system model, sphinx-needs for
requirements and traces, zdocs for a linked document set, and west for the workspace. Its one
tool is `curatrix`.

XDMOD gives you three things:

1. **One trace graph across all domains.** Every need, model element, CAD part, code unit and
   test result has an ID, and the more concrete side holds each link. Checks find broken, missing
   and suspect links, in every repo and across the full set.
2. **Documents that come from the design.** Requirements, architecture, CAD and code produce one
   linked, versioned document set. Generated content is committed and checked, so it can’t drift.
3. **One workflow for humans and agents.** The same commands, checks and reviews apply to
   everyone. Agents propose; only a human’s commit affirms.

Examples in this manual come from the robot arm, the worked example of XDMOD. Every page reads
on its own without it.

## How to read this manual

The manual follows Diátaxis:

- [Tutorials](tutorials/index.html.md) walk you through your first workspace, requirement and change.
- [How-to guides](howto/index.html.md) are short recipes for one task each.
- [Reference](reference/index.html.md) lists the facts: trace model, ID scheme, checks, layouts.
- [Explanation](explanation/index.html.md) says why things are the way they are, and holds every framework
  decision and method rule as a need.

The command line and the Sphinx extensions are documented in the curatrix reference
(`xdmod-ref`).

For agents and other tools, the build also writes `llms.txt` (a list of all pages),
`llms-full.txt` (all pages in one file) and a Markdown copy of every page (`<page>.md`) next
to the HTML ([*Agent-readable docs with sp... (XD-ADR-0111)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0111)). The needs themselves are best read from `needs.json`.

| Framework Decision: **Checks that bite** [XD-ADR-0125](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0125)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>   |

| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>decides: [XD-RULE-0045](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0045), [XD-RULE-0046](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0046)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **A check run passes only if it checked something** (Phase 4 review P4-4, P4-14; plan Phase 5, task 5.1). A missing `checks.yaml` and an empty plan fail. Each repo lists the checks it runs in `expect:`, so a lost section is an error (CK-H6); `curatrix check` prints the checks that are off and why. An error-level check that is skipped at the baseline stage fails. Failures of git and west are reported, never treated as “nothing found”. A pull request gets a warning when it changes more than 600 hand-written lines or 15 files against its base (CK-H7): one SYSMOD step or one tool feature per PR.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refines: [XD-ADR-0051](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051), [XD-ADR-0123](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0123)<br/><br/><br/>decides: [XD-RULE-0051](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0051), [XD-RULE-0052](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0052), [XD-RULE-0061](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0061), [XD-RULE-0062](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0062)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Accepted CAD findings live in one file format for EE and ME:** `pcba/<name>/accepted.yaml` and<br/>`assemblies/<name>/accepted.yaml`, read by the same check code. An entry names the check, the<br/>rule, the items (designators or part names, never positions, so the entry survives a move; or all<br/>findings of one rule, as for unrouted nets) and the reason.<br/><br/>**Only a human accepts.** An entry counts as accepted only when the commit that added it carries an<br/>explicit `Accepted-by: <name>` trailer, has no agent trailer, and changes nothing but acceptance<br/>entries. Agents never write `Accepted-by:`; an entry from an agent commit, or not yet committed,<br/>is a proposal ([*Only a human's commit affirms (XD-ADR-0051)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051)): a warning locally, an error at the baseline. Real enforcement<br/>(commits signed with a key only the owner holds) stays in iteration 2 ([*Agent limits are policy onl... (XD-ADR-0123)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0123)).<br/><br/>- Only errors must be accepted; warnings are listed and never fail.<br/>- KiCad’s own exclusions stay for single, stable findings, under the same rule: an exclusion<br/>  counts as accepted only when the commit that added it to the `.kicad_pro` carries<br/>  `Accepted-by:`, has no agent trailer and changes nothing but exclusions or acceptance entries;<br/>  otherwise it is a proposal. Stated rule: a KiCad exclusion is lost when its items move. An ERC exclusion counts only if no finding of the same type and items is<br/>  reported as not excluded, because KiCad turns a stale ERC exclusion into an excluded phantom<br/>  finding (KiCad spike §4.4).<br/>- A board’s ERC and DRC severities must equal those of the `curatrix new pcba` template (a<br/>  missing `erc` section counts as KiCad’s defaults). A difference is a finding that needs<br/>  acceptance, so a severity cannot silently switch a rule off.<br/>- The reports stay local; CI and Pages show a placeholder in the findings section. |

# explanation/decisions/domains.html.md

<a id="adr-domains"></a>

# Domain models and CAD

How the EE and ME repos refine the system model, which needs their models emit, and how KiCad
and FreeCAD files refer to them (Phase 5, task 5.14). Decisions that rest on the FreeCAD spike are
*proposed* until that spike is merged.

<a id="XD-ADR-0130"></a>

| Framework Decision: **Domain repos refine the system model by specialization** [XD-ADR-0130](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0130)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refines: [XD-ADR-0030](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0030)<br/><br/><br/>refined by: [XD-ADR-0132](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0132), [XD-ADR-0137](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0137)<br/><br/><br/>decides: [XD-RULE-0047](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0047)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **The EE and ME repos each have their own SysML model in** `model/` **and refine the system<br/>model by specialization.** SW keeps its architecture in rst in iteration 1 ([*SW architecture in rst in i... (XD-ADR-0069)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0069));<br/>a SW sub-model would follow the same pattern in iteration 2. There are three levels of detail:<br/><br/>- **System model** (the systems engineering repo): what crosses a domain boundary. Blocks down to<br/>  the product level (one part def per board, assembly and SW component), their ports, and the<br/>  interface defs (`SYS-IF`) at signal level: signal names, direction, kind, values from the<br/>  requirements. No connector types, pin numbers or part numbers.<br/>- **Domain model** (`<domain repo>/model/`): how the domain realizes a block. EE: board defs,<br/>  connector port defs with connector type and pin map (pin number and net name per signal), cable<br/>  defs, external parts, board variants. ME: assembly and sub-assembly defs, mechanical port defs<br/>  with geometry, assembly variants. In iteration 1 there are no circuit block diagrams inside a<br/>  board.<br/>- **Implementation** (KiCad projects, WireViz files, FreeCAD documents): they name the domain<br/>  model elements they implement.<br/><br/>A domain def specializes the system def it realizes (`part def JointControllerBoard :><br/>JointController`) and redefines every inherited port with a port whose def specializes the<br/>interface def (`port def ServoHeader :> ServoIf`). A domain def may specialize several system<br/>defs; a name clash between inherited ports is solved by one port that redefines all of them<br/>(`port :>> A::p, B::p : X;`). Redefined signal ports repeat their direction (`out port :>><br/>pwm`). Inside a def that specializes a system def, outer elements are named by qualified name,<br/>because inherited members hide outer names.<br/><br/>A domain model imports only the system model and the xdmod libraries; SW reads the EE model<br/>([*SW reads the board pin maps... (XD-ADR-0131)*](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0131)). It reads the upstream model twice, both from the same west pin: as a<br/>library set for the Pilot, and as the upstream’s committed `generated/model.json` for the<br/>checks that run without Java. The repo’s own model files are read as one set, so their order does<br/>not matter. Each domain model costs one more Pilot run; the owner accepted that. Based on the<br/>model spike (`claude/notes/model-spike.md`). |

<a id="XD-ADR-0132"></a>

| Framework Decision: **curatrix checks conformance and derives the links** [XD-ADR-0132](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0132)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refines: [XD-ADR-0130](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0130)<br/><br/><br/>decides: [XD-RULE-0047](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0047)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Conformance is a curatrix check, not a Pilot result.** The Pilot finds neither a missing<br/>redefinition nor a redefinition with the wrong port def. So curatrix checks, on the committed<br/>model JSON of the domain repo and its upstream: every port that a domain def inherits from a<br/>system def is redefined somewhere in the chain between the two, and the most specific<br/>redefinition’s def specializes the inherited port’s def. The same rule holds inside port defs at<br/>signal level. A variant def of a board does not repeat the redefinitions of its parent. An<br/>unsolved name clash of inherited ports is an error.<br/><br/>**Links come from specialization.** `curatrix gen model` turns a `:>` across the repo boundary<br/>into a trace link on the domain need, chosen by the pair of kinds: `EE-PCBA` / `ME-ASM` /<br/>`EE-HAR` to `SYS-EL` is `realizes`; `EE-PORT` / `ME-PORT` to `SYS-IF` is `conforms`.<br/>Any other pair is a finding, never skipped. A def without an ID of its own that specializes a<br/>system element is allowed only below the port level (for example a signal def inside a port def);<br/>anywhere else it is a warning. |

<a id="XD-ADR-0128"></a>

| Framework Decision: **The domain model owns the IDs of boards, assemblies, ports and harnesses** [XD-ADR-0128](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0128)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refined by: [XD-ADR-0139](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0139)<br/><br/><br/>revises: [XD-ADR-0023](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0023)<br/><br/><br/>decides: [XD-RULE-0049](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0049), [XD-RULE-0050](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0050), [XD-RULE-0055](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0055)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **The domain model emits the** `EE-PCBA`, `EE-PORT`, `EE-HAR`, `ME-ASM` **and**<br/>`ME-PORT` **needs.** The ID is the short name of the def in the domain model. KiCad, WireViz and<br/>FreeCAD files carry these IDs only as references: the `TraceID` of a KiCad project or of the top<br/>FreeCAD document of an assembly, the `Port` field of a KiCad connector, the `Port` property of<br/>a FreeCAD LCS, the port names at both ends of a harness. The `Realizes` and `Conforms` fields on<br/>KiCad projects and FreeCAD documents go away: these links are derived from specialization<br/>([*curatrix checks conformance... (XD-ADR-0132)*](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0132)). `EE-CMP` and `ME-PART` stay owned by the CAD files, as before<br/>([*Trace IDs live inside the C... (XD-ADR-0023)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0023)).<br/><br/>**One CAD file per domain def.** Each board def has exactly one KiCad project<br/>`pcba/<name>/<name>.kicad_pro`, each cable def exactly one harness folder `harness/<name>/`, each<br/>assembly or sub-assembly def exactly one FreeCAD document; and each of these files names exactly<br/>one def. The folder name comes from the element name (`JointController` →<br/>`joint-controller`). The project’s entry point is its `.kicad_pro`; the root schematic has the<br/>same name. Instances are usages of the def, in any number; the trace stays on the def<br/>([*The definition holds the tr... (XD-ADR-0117)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0117)). A single ME part is 1:1 with a model element only when the model treats it<br/>as a block. The CK-D4 readers change with this decision. |

| Framework Decision: **Need kinds EE-PORT, ME-PORT and EE-HAR** [XD-ADR-0133](explanation/decisions/domains.html.md#XD-ADR-0133)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refines: [XD-ADR-0030](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0030)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Three new need kinds.**<br/><br/>- `EE-PORT`: a connector port of a board, or a port of an external part, in the EE model. It<br/>  `conforms` to the `SYS-IF` it specializes and is `part_of` its board (`EE-PCBA`). A port<br/>  of an external part has no `part_of`; its qualified name names the part. A KiCad connector<br/>  names it in its `Port` field; a connector without a port says so with `Port = -`.<br/>- `ME-PORT`: a mechanical interface of an assembly in the ME model, with its geometry. It<br/>  `conforms` to the `SYS-IF` it specializes and is `part_of` its assembly (`ME-ASM`). In<br/>  FreeCAD it is an LCS with a `Port` property.<br/>- `EE-HAR`: a wiring harness, 1:1 with a cable def in the EE model. It `connects` the two or more<br/>  `EE-PORT` s its ends mate with. The harness is built to fit those ports, so it is the more<br/>  concrete side and holds the link ([*Trace rule: the concrete si... (XD-ADR-0004)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0004)). Like every design element it must<br/>  `realizes` a `SYS-EL` or `satisfies` an `EE-REQ` (no orphans, [*No orphan design elements (XD-RULE-0010)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0010)); it may<br/>  also `conforms` to a `SYS-IF`. Ports are not in the orphan rule: a port of an external part<br/>  may conform to nothing. |

| **Second exception to the peer rule: ME may write into EE’s KiCad project, but only inside a<br/>co-design change.** The space a board may take is a `SYS-IF` budget in the system model: a port<br/>def with a box (`width`, `depth`, `heightAbove`, `heightBelow`), a hole list<br/>(`hole<n>X`, `hole<n>Y`, `holeDiameter`) and connector positions (`<ref>X`, `<ref>Y`,<br/>pin 1), in the board frame (origin at the lower-left corner of the outline seen from the top, x<br/>right, y up, z = 0 on the top face). StepUp is pinned by commit under `.xdmod/stepup/` (pin and licence gap:<br/>[Make a co-design change (ME and EE)](howto/co-design-change.html.md#howto-co-design-change)). The EE side reviews and merges its part. ME never takes<br/>EE geometry outside such a change, and ME needs never link to EE needs.<br/><br/>**Scope in iteration 1** (co-design spike, `claude/notes/codesign-spike.md`): keep-out zones<br/>are not pushed (the box covers the space; StepUp could push them, iteration 2). Connector<br/>positions are budget values, but never pushed: EE places connectors, and a planned check (task<br/>5.25) compares them. | **Each top-level assembly is a folder** `assemblies/<name>/` with its top document<br/>`<name>.FCStd`, a skeleton document `skeleton.FCStd`, and its own parts; shared parts stay in<br/>`parts/`. The skeleton holds the parameter spreadsheet `Params` and the master sketch. The<br/>master sketch cannot live in the top document: parts that refer to it would form a document cycle,<br/>and FreeCAD then recomputes in an undefined order (FreeCAD spike §1). Parts refer only to the<br/>skeleton, never to the top document; the top document links the skeleton and the parts. At most ten<br/>driving parameters in iteration 1.<br/><br/>**The model drives the CAD.** `curatrix gen freecad-params` writes the model values into<br/>`Params` (aliases `<port>_<attribute>`): it opens the top document first, writes values only<br/>(it never rebuilds objects, so object IDs do not churn), recomputes skeleton, parts, sub-assemblies<br/>and top in this order, and saves only the documents whose values changed. CK-F3 checks that they<br/>agree.<br/><br/>**Interfaces** are LCS with a `Port` property (the `ME-PORT` ID). **Variants** are rows of a<br/>configuration table in `Params` plus `Configs` on the links; part presence comes from<br/>`Configs`, never from a suppressed state. Checks, value writes and the exploded view run in<br/>`FreeCADCmd`. The exploded view uses the fallback of the FreeCAD spike (§5): the moves are data<br/>(a small table per assembly, or read from the `Move` objects in `Document.xml`), and a script<br/>builds the exploded compound and its TechDraw view; the Assembly workbench’s exploded view in the<br/>GUI binary hung in 6 of 8 runs, so it is only a design aid. Only full TechDraw pages and StepUp<br/>need the GUI binary with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`; task 5.26 first shows that the page export<br/>runs reliably, or falls back to view SVGs. Both run through curatrix with the workspace-local<br/>configuration. Based on the FreeCAD spike (`claude/notes/freecad-spike.md`). |

# explanation/decisions/index.html.md

<a id="adr-index"></a>

# Decisions

This part records every decision about the XDMOD framework. Each decision is a need of type
`xd-adr` (an *architecture decision record*), with an ID `XD-ADR-nnnn` from xdmod’s ledger
`ids.yaml`. Decisions that are only about one project that uses XDMOD (its hardware, its repos,
its GitHub settings, its licence) are kept in that project’s own documents, as `prj-dec` needs.
A project decision may `follows` a framework decision; a framework decision never links to a
project.

## How to read a decision

- `legacy_id` is the number the decision had in the planning log (`D1` to `D142`) before it
  became a need. Old texts and commit messages use these numbers.
- `date` is the day it was made.
- `decision_status` is `proposed` (written, but waiting for a spike or the owner), `accepted`, `revised` (a newer decision changed part of it) or
  `superseded` (a newer decision replaced it). Changed decisions are never deleted or edited
  into something new: they keep their need, and the newer decision holds the link to them
  (`refines`, `revises` or `supersedes`). The older need shows the link back as
  “refined by”, “revised by” or “superseded by”. This is the trace rule
  [*Trace rule: the concrete si... (XD-ADR-0004)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0004) applied to decisions.
- Rules that a decision introduces are `xd-rule` needs that are `decided_by` it (see
  [Rules](explanation/rules/index.html.md)).

## How to add a decision

1. Add an `xd-adr` need to the topic page it fits, with a placeholder ID
   (`<KIND>-NEW-<tag>`, see the ID scheme), `decision_status: accepted`, `status: valid` and today’s `date`.
2. If it changes an older decision, add `refines`, `revises` or `supersedes` with the older
   ID, and set the older need’s `decision_status`.
3. Run `curatrix ids fix xdmod` to issue the ID, then `curatrix check xdmod --stage local`.

<a id="XD-ADR-0145"></a>

| Framework Decision: **KiCad and FreeCAD never run outside curatrix; shims in .venv/bin** [XD-ADR-0145](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0145)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>date: 2026-11-17<br/><br/><br/>decision_status: accepted<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>refines: [XD-ADR-0080](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0080)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Never run KiCad or FreeCAD outside curatrix or its shims, not even** `--version`. A bare<br/>`kicad-cli --version` rewrites `~/.config/kicad/10.0/kicad_common.json`; agents did this twice.<br/>As a safety net, `curatrix bootstrap` and `update` write shims into the main workspace’s<br/>`.venv/bin` (also when run from a worktree set) for every KiCad and FreeCAD program on the machine:<br/>`kicad-cli`, `kicad`, `eeschema`, `pcbnew`, `bitmap2component`, each program with a KiCad<br/>`.kiface` (`gerbview`, `pl_editor`, `pcb_calculator`, …) and every `freecad*` program in any<br/>case (`FreeCAD`, `FreeCADCmd`, `freecad`, `freecadcmd`, …). A shim sets the workspace-local<br/>config that `curatrix run` sets (`LC_ALL` only for `kicad-cli`; the GUIs keep the user’s<br/>locale) and runs the real binary, found by absolute path when the shim is written (never<br/>`.venv/bin` itself or another shim). KiCad’s IDF converters (`idfcyl`, `dxf2idf`, …) write no<br/>config and get no shim. `curatrix env` puts `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`; `curatrix doctor` warns when<br/>a KiCad or FreeCAD name on `PATH` is not the shim, or a shim’s real binary is gone. Nothing outside the workspace changes: no<br/>user-global files, no `PATH` edits in shell profiles. The shims set no limits, so the tools still<br/>run through curatrix ([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064)). |

(XD-ADR-0140)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0140)). A job can name a<br/>  variant (KiCad 10.0.8, KiCad spike §2.2), so the jobset holds one job per variant-dependent output<br/>  and variant, copied from its base job except for the variant and file name; the variant names in<br/>  the jobs equal those of the project. No “Execute Command” jobs, no “Copy Files” outside the<br/>  output folder, no statistics job, BOM delimiters set, ERC and DRC not in the jobset (the checks<br/>  evaluate them). curatrix fails the run when fewer jobs ran than the jobset has (a job KiCad<br/>  cannot parse drops all jobs with exit code 0).<br/>- **Outputs:** Gerber and drill, pick-and-place, netlist, STEP, top and bottom renderings<br/>  (orthographic) and one 3D rendering, schematic PDF and SVG, BOM CSV. | Proposed by the agent of task 5.30, for the owner to accept or change. The spike<br/>(`claude/notes/me-renderings-spike.md`) found that neither the Render workbench (an addon that<br/>needs an external renderer) nor a Coin3D snapshot (`saveImage` in the GUI binary offscreen gives a<br/>blank image; `SoOffscreenRenderer` finds no GL context) works headless. Time grows with the drawn pixels and the facet count: 4 to 8 s per view<br/>for 272 000 facets (60 filleted tubes), about 1 s per view for a few boxes, on the owner’s machine,<br/>well inside the `freecad` limit of 10 minutes for a few variants. |

# Workflow and agents

Branches, merging, reviews, and what agents may do.

| **Merging:** trunk-based on `main`. Every change goes through a PR, required checks must pass, and PRs are **rebase-merged** (linear history). The user’s review and merge is the approval.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

# explanation/humans-and-agents.html.md

<a id="expl-humans-and-agents"></a>

# Humans and agents

In XDMOD, AI agents are first-class: they author and review design content the same way human
engineers do, with the same tools ([*Agents are first-class (XD-ADR-0003)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0003)). The difference is who may **decide**.

## Roles

| Role              | Who                                    | Does                                                                                                        |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Owner             | a person                               | sets goals, makes decisions, reviews and merges every PR, affirms evidence, makes baselines                 |
| Domain engineer   | a person (SE, EE, ME, SW, integration) | authors and reviews content in their domain; affirms suspect links in their domain                          |
| Agent author      | an AI agent                            | authors content on a branch (requirements, model, CAD through scripts, code, tests,<br/>docs) and opens PRs |
| Agent reviewer    | an AI agent, not the author            | first-pass review of a PR against checklists; posts findings as PR comments                                 |
| Coordinator agent | the agent the owner talks to           | plans, splits work, starts other agents, gathers results, keeps the plan and the<br/>decision log           |

## Propose versus affirm

Agents analyse suspect links and prepare affirmations and verdicts. But **only a person’s commit
counts** as an affirmation or a verdict ([*Only a human's commit affirms (XD-ADR-0051)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051)). The same holds for merging: the owner’s
review and merge is the approval ([*Agents work under the user'... (XD-ADR-0044)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0044)).

## What agents may and may not do

| Agents may                                                                                                                                                                                 | Agents may not                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| create branches, commit, push to their own branches                                                                                                                                        | merge PRs, push to `main`, force-push to other people’s branches                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| open PRs and issues and comment on them, with the provenance trailer ([*Provenance trailer on GitHu... (XD-ADR-0065)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0065))           | change repo or org settings, rulesets or secrets, or create or delete repos, without the<br/>owner’s approval of the concrete action list ([*GitHub admin by agents only... (XD-ADR-0112)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0112)) |
| add `Co-Authored-By`, and `Signed-off-by` in the owner’s name where a repo requires<br/>it ([*Sign-off by agents (XD-ADR-0108)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0108)) | affirm suspect links or give manual verdicts; they only propose them ([*Only a human's commit affirms (XD-ADR-0051)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0051))                                                                       |
| run any tool through curatrix, under limits ([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064))                                    | run tools without limits, install system packages, use sudo                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| record HIL evidence from `main` or baseline commits ([*Evidence only from main or ... (XD-ADR-0053)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0053))                            | record evidence from PR branches as anything but previews                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| post freely in the project’s own repos and in xdmod                                                                                                                                        | post on other repos (doc engine, tools, upstream projects) before the owner approved the<br/>draft ([*Posting approval outside ou... (XD-ADR-0113)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0113))                                        |

These limits are policy in iteration 1: agents work under the owner’s GitHub account
([*Agent limits are policy onl... (XD-ADR-0123)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0123)).

## Provenance

Every agent commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer ([*Agents work under the user'... (XD-ADR-0044)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0044), [*Agent commits carry a trailer (XD-RULE-0042)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0042)). Everything an
agent posts on GitHub (issues, comments, PR texts, reviews) ends with the line
`🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` ([*Provenance trailer on GitHu... (XD-ADR-0065)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0065)). The check
[*commit trailers on agent co... (XD-CHECK-0028)*](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0028) warns about commits without the trailer.

## Review by another agent

Every pull request in the project repos and in xdmod gets a review by an agent other than the
author, before the owner’s review ([*Every PR gets an agent review (XD-ADR-0115)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0115)).

## Working in parallel

Several agents can work at the same time. Two agents never edit the same repo checkout at once.
An agent that changes repos works in its own **git worktrees** under
`<ws>/.worktrees/<branch>/<repo>`, made with `curatrix work start` ([*Parallel agents work in git... (XD-ADR-0114)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0114)). Shared,
read-only parts (Zephyr, libraries, `.venv`) are not duplicated.

Each agent gets a short brief: its goal, the decisions that bind it, the files to read, its
output paths, and what it must not do. It returns a short report; the coordinator checks the
claims that matter before passing them on.

## Agent material in the repos

Each repo has a `claude/` folder with its own rules, skills and pitfalls ([*Agent material in each repo... (XD-ADR-0062)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0062)). xdmod
holds the launch `CLAUDE.md` for the workspace root, and shared skills, commands and checklists.
The bootstrap copies the launch file to the root and links all skills and commands into
`<workspace>/.claude/` ([*The bootstrap assembles .cl... (XD-ADR-0103)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0103)). See [Repo layouts](reference/repo-layouts.html.md).

# explanation/multi-repo.html.md

<a id="expl-multi-repo"></a>

# Many repos, one workspace

An XDMOD project lives in several git repos: one per engineering domain, one for integration,
one manifest, and the framework itself. They are managed together as one **west workspace**
([*A multi-repo workspace with... (XD-ADR-0006)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0006)).

## Why several repos

Each domain has its own tools, reviewers and pace. Separate repos keep their histories, checks
and permissions apart, while the trace links still connect them. Example (robot arm): the repos
`robarm-syseng`, `robarm-ee`, `robarm-me`, `robarm-sw` and `robarm-integration`, with
`robarm-manifest` as the manifest and `xdmod` as the framework ([*Names: XDMOD, -trix tools, ... (XD-ADR-0042)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0042)).

- The **systems engineering** repo holds needs, requirements, the SysML model and views. It is
  upstream of every domain.
- Each **domain** repo (EE, ME, SW) holds its requirements, design and domain tests.
- The **integration** repo holds the system and integration tests, the HIL setups and the
  orphan evidence branch ([*An integration repo for sys... (XD-ADR-0066)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0066)). A test that verifies a system requirement or an interface
  lives there, even if it touches one domain only ([*Tests live by what they verify (XD-ADR-0104)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0104)).
- The **manifest** repo pins every other repo ([*A dedicated manifest repo (XD-ADR-0011)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0011)), builds the full document set, and
  holds the baselines.
- **xdmod** is in every workspace that uses the framework ([*xdmod is in every workspace (XD-ADR-0059)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0059)).

## The manifest pins everything

The manifest repo is the **only** place that pins revisions ([*The manifest is the only pl... (XD-ADR-0033)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0033)). Framework and design
repos and libraries are pinned by commit SHA; third-party trees such as Zephyr may be pinned by
tag. No other repo has its own `west.yml`.

The manifest is split into **submanifests**, one per area, and its projects carry **groups**
([*West submanifests and proje... (XD-ADR-0079)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0079)). Each role checks out only what it needs, through west’s group filter. The default
filter is minimal: framework, systems engineering and Zephyr ([*A minimal default group filter (XD-ADR-0084)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0084)). A role always gets its
upstream repos and the framework. The integration role gets everything except the big CAD
libraries ([*The integration role (XD-ADR-0082)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0082)). Component libraries are pinned west projects too, isolated from any
user-global setup ([*Pinned, isolated component ... (XD-ADR-0080)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0080)).

West rule to remember: a project is active as soon as **one** of its groups is enabled. So a big
library carries only its own group, never also the domain group.

## One workspace root

The workspace root is the west topdir ([*One west topdir at the work... (XD-ADR-0061)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0061)). It holds `.west/`, `.venv/`, `build/`
and all repos. Design repos sit at the top level; dependencies go under `tools/` and `libs/`
([*Workspace paths (XD-ADR-0083)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0083)). Every command runs from the root ([*All commands run from the w... (XD-ADR-0060)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0060)). See [Workspace](reference/workspace.html.md).

## A change across repos

1. **One branch name** in every repo the change touches ([*One branch name across repos (XD-ADR-0045)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0045)).
2. **One pull request per repo.** Each lists its sibling PRs.
3. **PR CI** checks each repo against its siblings. For each sibling it takes, in this order: a
   branch with the same name; the repo’s `main` if the manifest pin is an ancestor of it; the
   manifest pin ([*PR CI sibling resolution (XD-ADR-0116)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0116)). So downstream PRs see upstream changes that are merged but not yet
   bumped.
4. **Merge upstream first**: systems engineering, then the domains, then integration. Framework
   changes merge before the repos that use them. Every PR is rebase-merged ([*Trunk-based merging with re... (XD-ADR-0043)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0043)).
5. **Bump bot.** A scheduled job in the manifest repo compares each repo’s `main` with its pin
   and opens or updates one bump PR ([*A bump bot for manifest pins (XD-ADR-0054)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0054), [*The bump bot is a scheduled... (XD-ADR-0081)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0081)). Because a PR opened with the job’s
   own token does not trigger CI, the job builds the full set itself and reports on the PR.

## Baselines and bundles

A **baseline** is a tag `baseline/vX.Y.Z` of the manifest repo: a fixed set of repo versions
([*Terms: baseline and bundle (XD-ADR-0034)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0034), [*SemVer tags and baseline tags (XD-ADR-0047)*](explanation/decisions/repos.html.md#XD-ADR-0047)). A **bundle** is the package of outputs built from one baseline: docs,
CAM data, firmware, HIL results. Bundles come in iteration 2 ([*Scope moved to iteration 2 (XD-ADR-0037)*](explanation/decisions/scope.html.md#XD-ADR-0037)).

Before a baseline is tagged, the gates run: no links to retired needs ([*Links to retired needs are ... (XD-RULE-0011)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0011)), no open suspect
links ([*Suspect links are reviewed ... (XD-RULE-0014)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0014)), and a full local build with CAD content. The documentation is published on
GitHub Pages of the manifest repo, with `main` as “latest” and one folder per baseline
([*Docs hosting on GitHub Page... (XD-ADR-0048)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0048)).

## Documents across repos

Each repo has its own zdocs registry ([*One zdocs registry per repo... (XD-ADR-0021)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0021)), which also builds its upstream documents
locally from the west checkout, so links into upstream needs resolve ([*Upstream documents are buil... (XD-ADR-0029)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0029)). The manifest
repo’s registry builds the full linked set. The XDMOD manual is part of that set; project
documents link to the manual, but the manual never links to a project ([*The XDMOD manual is part of... (XD-ADR-0101)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0101)).


# explanation/principles.html.md

<a id="expl-principles"></a>

# Principles

XDMOD rests on a few ideas. Most rules in this manual follow from them.

## The concrete side holds the link

A trace link is written on the **more concrete** artifact and points to the more abstract one
([*Trace rule: the concrete si... (XD-ADR-0004)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0004), refined by [*Link-type table and interfa... (XD-ADR-0030)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0030)). In the V-model, links point from right to left and from
bottom to top: a test case says what it verifies, a design element says what it realizes, a
domain requirement says what it refines. The abstract side never lists its children. Backlinks
such as “refined by” or “verified by” are only ever computed by the tools ([*The concrete side holds the... (XD-RULE-0001)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0001)).

Why? The concrete artifact is the one that changes most often, and its author knows what it is
for. An upstream document stays stable while downstream work goes on, and many repos can add
links to it in parallel without touching it.

Each link type belongs to the need type that owns it ([*Link types are declared on ... (XD-RULE-0002)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0002)). There is no global link
table. A link written on the wrong side, to an unknown ID or to a wrong target type fails the
build. Peer domains (for example EE and SW) never link to each other: they both link to a shared
interface need in the systems engineering repo ([*Peer interfaces live in sys... (XD-RULE-0003)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0003)). Allocation is stored on the concrete
side, too ([*Allocation is stored on the... (XD-RULE-0004)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0004)).

## Generate, commit, check

Many files are made by tools: SysML stubs for requirements, needs extracted from the model and
from CAD files, views of the model. XDMOD **commits** these files and **checks** that they still
match their sources ([*Generated files are committ... (XD-RULE-0033)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0033)). That has three benefits:

- Reviewers see the generated change in the pull request, next to the change that caused it.
- CI does not need the heavy tools (Java, KiCad, FreeCAD) to see the full trace graph
  ([*CAD-derived needs are commi... (XD-ADR-0100)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0100)).
- A stale file is a check failure, not a silent error.

Generated needs follow the same rules as authored needs ([*Generated needs follow the ... (XD-RULE-0006)*](explanation/rules/trace.html.md#XD-RULE-0006)).

## Text first, for people and agents

Everything that people review is text in git: reStructuredText for needs and documents
([*Requirements in sphinx-needs (XD-ADR-0005)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0005)), SysML v2 textual notation for the model ([*SysML v2 textual notation f... (XD-ADR-0001)*](explanation/decisions/method.html.md#XD-ADR-0001)), uncompressed FreeCAD files
and drawio views ([*Design files are stored unc... (XD-RULE-0039)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0039)). Agents edit and review this content the same way engineers do
([*Agents are first-class (XD-ADR-0003)*](explanation/decisions/workflow.html.md#XD-ADR-0003)). Diffs are readable, merges are possible, and every change goes through a pull
request.

## Documents come from the models

Documents pull content out of the design models, the way API documentation comes from code
comments ([*Documents extract content f... (XD-ADR-0017)*](explanation/decisions/documents.html.md#XD-ADR-0017)). Authored rst gives the structure and the prose; Sphinx extensions add
tables, pictures and needs from SysML, KiCad, FreeCAD, code and test results.

## Every check runs locally

Every check that CI runs can also run on your machine, with one command per repo, from the
workspace root ([*Every check also runs locally (XD-ADR-0040)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0040), [*Every check runs locally (XD-RULE-0032)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0032)). Every tool runs under a memory limit and a timeout
([*A memory limit and a timeou... (XD-ADR-0064)*](explanation/decisions/checks.html.md#XD-ADR-0064), [*Every tool runs under limits (XD-RULE-0044)*](explanation/rules/checks.html.md#XD-RULE-0044)), so a runaway tool cannot stall the machine or other agents.

## IDs are stable

Every need has an ID like `SYS-REQ-0012` from the repo’s ledger ([*ID format DOMAIN-KIND-NNNN (XD-ADR-0071)*](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0071)). An ID never
changes when its need is renamed or moved, and it is never issued again ([*IDs are never reused; retir... (XD-RULE-0020)*](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0020)). See
[ID scheme](reference/id-scheme.html.md).

# ID rules

Rules for IDs and the ledger.

| status: valid<br/><br/><br/>tags: ids<br/><br/><br/>legacy_id: id-scheme 6.1<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>decided by: [XD-ADR-0071](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0071), [XD-ADR-0109](explanation/decisions/traces.html.md#XD-ADR-0109)<br/><br/><br/>enforced by: [XD-CHECK-0003](reference/checks.html.md#XD-CHECK-0003)<br/><br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

<a id="XD-RULE-0016"></a>

| Method Rule: **IDs are unique** [XD-RULE-0016](explanation/rules/ids.html.md#XD-RULE-0016)  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-down-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="8 12 12 16 16 12"></polyline><line x1="12" y1="8" x2="12" y2="16"></line></svg><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="feather feather-arrow-right-circle"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle><polyline points="12 16 16 12 12 8"></polyline><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="16" y2="12"></line></svg> <br/><br/>   |

# explanation/rules/index.html.md

<a id="rules-index"></a>

# Rules

The XDMOD method has rules: how links are written, how IDs are issued, how variants are bound,
and how repos are kept clean. Each rule is a need of type `xd-rule` with an ID
`XD-RULE-nnnn`. Each rule is `decided_by` the decision (`xd-adr`) that introduced it, and
each curatrix check that enforces a rule is an `xd-check` need that `enforces` it (see
[Checks](reference/checks.html.md)). So for every rule you can see why it exists and which check
catches a break of it. A rule without an “enforced by” link is followed by convention or by the
tools themselves, not by a check.

`legacy_id` is the name the rule had in the planning drafts, for example `R3` or `V4`, or
the place in the draft it comes from.

* [Trace rules](explanation/rules/trace.html.md)
* [ID rules](explanation/rules/ids.html.md)
* [Variant rules](explanation/rules/variants.html.md)
* [Check principles](explanation/rules/checks.html.md)
